API and examples

Documentation from source commit b167b55c1cd0 · 2026-11-05. Source documentation can include work beyond the registry release.

Read the package documentation

Revision-safe operations for an editing workspace. One coordinator serializes generation and editing, captures the requested document revision, and rejects late answers after edits, document/account changes, cancellation or disposal.

The package supports authoring adapters such as OrangeCat article editing, BiasLens source rewrites and Heidi language-learning adaptations. Product package plans record actual adoption. The package has no runtime dependencies.

Use

import { WritingSession } from '@bitbaum/writingkit';

const session = new WritingSession({ documentId, revision });
// On every committed edit, advance the host revision and synchronize it.
session.update({ documentId, revision: nextRevision });

// Capture the text and host options before the asynchronous operation starts.
const input = { ...currentDraft };
const outcome = await session.run(
  ({ signal, base }) => proposeEdit({ input, base, signal }),
  proposal => {
    applyToEditor(proposal);
  }
);

if (outcome.status === 'stale') showWritingChanged();
if (outcome.status === 'failed') showRetry(outcome.error);
// busy/cancelled outcomes must not replace the current workspace's messages.
session.cancel(); // invalidates the answer even if the provider ignores abort
session.dispose(); // permanently closes this owner when the workspace is removed

run reserves the workspace synchronously, before the first await. Its apply callback runs only after validation and must be synchronous. Its undefined return type rejects asynchronous callbacks in TypeScript; use a block callback as above. The callback may advance the host revision after applying the edit. It should commit the proposed fields together rather than partly applying them.

The document identity is an opaque host key. Include the account/tenant boundary where a draft id alone is not unique. Never treat that string as authorization. Revision tokens can be numbers or strings; an internal epoch also detects a token changed and then restored. Call update for every committed edit, even if the text later returns to its previous value. Repeating the same revision is a no-op. A document change aborts the old operation and frees the workspace for the new one immediately. A same-document edit keeps the operation reserved until completion or explicit cancellation, then reports stale.

Create a fresh session per editor lifecycle. In React, create it inside the owning layout-effect setup and dispose that instance in its cleanup. This also handles development Strict Mode's setup/cleanup replay. Synchronize committed revisions in a layout effect, before a pending answer can run between commit and passive-effect cleanup. UI busy/error state stays with the host; a cancelled old operation must not clear a newer operation's busy state (session.busy).

Ownership

Hosts own the document, immutable original source, proposed edits and Undo, version history, labels/citations, language/variety checks, account storage, server authorization, quotas and publication. Model/HTTP execution remains in the host's existing ai-kit/API adapter. Chat remains chatkit; published reading surfaces remain bip-kit. No provider, endpoint or language is selected here.

Cancellation does not undo a server-side write. Prefer operations that produce proposals. If an existing endpoint commits a revision before returning, retain its optimistic server revision checks and reconcile its result with server history even when the browser outcome is stale or cancelled. Never claim that this editing guard rolls back a database change.

Verification and ownership

From the package directory, install its declared development dependencies and run:

pnpm run verify

The package checks its types, builds its public exports and tests the actual exported runtime, including overlapping operations and late responses. Committed dist must match the build for the standalone package's GitHub install path.

Consumers install a verified package release; they do not import another product's source folder. During extraction, Fleet's package-repository workflow copies bootstrap source into its standalone repository. After creation, change the engine there and retire the bootstrap runtime copy and its temporary product verification binding on first adoption. Preserve the extraction commit as provenance. Product handoffs record the release/adoption state rather than this README claiming an unverified installation.
